items.q: An arterial gas shows low pH, low bicarbonate and low carbon dioxide. The primary disorder is?
o: Metabolic acidosis with respiratory compensation, then anion gap and cause hunt complete interpretation
Primary respiratory alkalosis
Normal gas needing no thought
Compensation that proves the lungs failed first
items.exp: Acid pH with low bicarbonate is metabolic acidosis. Low carbon dioxide is expected compensation. Gap and clinical cause decide danger and treatment (standard ABG teaching). Values are read from the patient chart; no numbers are memorised here.

items.q: Raised troponin in a patient with sepsis and kidney failure means what?
o: Myocardial injury needing ECG, story and trend interpretation, not automatic type one infarction labelling
Definite plaque rupture in every case
A laboratory error to ignore
No cardiac risk at all
items.exp: Troponin marks injury, not mechanism. Supply demand, renal clearance and true coronary events are separated by story, ECG and delta change (standard laboratory teaching; ESC principles).
